gloss: Liquid fat.
Petroleum-based liquid used as fuel or lubricant.
Petroleum.
An oil painting.
To lubricate with oil.
To grease with oil for cooking.
To fuel with oil.
To say in an unctuous manner.
Covered with or containing oil.
Resembling oil.
Excessively friendly or polite but insincere.
Representing the grunting sound made by a pig.
Drawing attention to male chauvinism (from the term male chauvinist pig).
The sound made by a pig, or an imitation thereof.
Of a pig or in imitation thereof, to make its characteristic sound.
A viscous preparation of oils and/or fats, usually containing medication, used as a treatment or as an emollient.
A substance used to anoint, as in religious rituals.
Cloth made from cotton and treated with oil and pigment to make it waterproof.
A raincoat made from cotton fabric treated with oil and pigment to make it waterproof.
Foul-weather gear worn by sailors, whether of natural or synthetic materials.
A painting done with oil paints.
The art of painting with oil paints.
A physically attractive person.
A hole drilled into the earth from which petroleum is pumped.
An industrial process plant where crude oil is processed and refined into useful petroleum products.
A fabric or cloth treated on one side with a waterproof covering, especially one made from linseed oil etc.; used for flooring, tablecloths, kitchen shelves and sometimes furniture covering.
The aromatic oil obtained from the berries of the wintergreen plant; mostly methyl salicylate; used medicinally and in perfumes
A container with a long spout, for holding oil and delivering it in drops or small quantities for lubrication.
A fragile spore produced by some fungi.
The fungus Erysiphe necator (= Uncinula necator), which produces powdery mildew in grapes.
A simple vessel used to produce light continuously for a period of time from a liquid fuel source, especially lamp oil.
A rig, consisting of a platform and machinery, used to drill for oil and other petroleum products, such as natural gas.
The industrial process of converting crude oil into petroleum and other useful products
The solid residue remaining after any oilseed has been pressed to remove the vegetable oil; it is used, with other ingredients, as animal food.
A cake made with vegetable oil instead of butter.
A nocturnal South American bird, of the species Steatornis caripensis of the order Steatornithiformes, related to the nightjars that feeds on the fruit of the oil palm and tropical laurels.
A plant of species Elaeis guineensis, principal source of palm oil and palm kernel oil.
Any species of palm which can usefully produce palm oil.
A department of Picardy, Hauts-de-France, France. Capital: Beauvais (INSEE code 60).
A right tributary of the Seine, originating in Belgium and flowing through the departments of Aisne, Oise, Val-d'Oise and Yvelines in northeastern France.

An escape or (accidental) discharge of oil, usually into the sea.
The process of draining old oil from an engine or gearbox and refilling it with fresh oil, often done at recommended intervals.
An active insecticide ingredient based on oil produced from the lemon eucalyptus (Corymbia citriodora), containing 64% or more of p-menthane-3,8-diol.
A pipeline that carries (crude) oil. (This entry is a translation hub.)
A ship that transports oil (petroleum), such as crude oil or bunker oil.
